ciaaw-weights.citation: CIAAW, Standard Atomic Weights 2024, www.ciaaw.org; T. Prohaska et al., Standard atomic weights of the elements 2021 (IUPAC Technical Report), Pure Appl. Chem. 2022, 94, 573–600.

ciaaw-abundances.citation: CIAAW, Isotopic Compositions of the Elements 2024, www.ciaaw.org; J. Meija et al., Isotopic compositions of the elements 2013 (IUPAC Technical Report), Pure Appl. Chem. 2016, 88, 293–306.

ame2020.citation: M. Wang, W. J. Huang, F. G. Kondev, G. Audi, S. Naimi, The AME 2020 atomic mass evaluation (II). Tables, graphs and references, Chin. Phys. C 2021, 45, 030003.

nubase2020.citation: F. G. Kondev, M. Wang, W. J. Huang, S. Naimi, G. Audi, The NUBASE2020 evaluation of nuclear physics properties, Chin. Phys. C 2021, 45, 030001.

nist-asd.citation: A. Kramida, Yu. Ralchenko, J. Reader, NIST ASD Team, NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12), NIST Standard Reference Database 78, National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD, 2024. DOI: 10.18434/T4W30F.

nist-srd144.citation: J. S. Coursey, D. J. Schwab, J. J. Tsai, R. A. Dragoset, Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions with Relative Atomic Masses (version 4.1, July 2015), NIST Standard Reference Database 144, National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD.

iaea-livechart.citation: IAEA Nuclear Data Section, Live Chart of Nuclides (ground states), International Atomic Energy Agency, Vienna.

ciaaw-abridged.citation: CIAAW, Abridged Standard Atomic Weights 2024, www.ciaaw.org; T. Prohaska et al., Standard atomic weights of the elements 2021 (IUPAC Technical Report), Pure Appl. Chem. 2022, 94, 573–600.

iupac-periodic-table.citation: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements (version 4 May 2022), International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry; abridged atomic weights as printed.

nist-periodic-table.citation: NIST, Periodic Table: Atomic Properties of the Elements, NIST Special Publication 966 (June 2024); atomic weights as printed.

pubchem.citation: S. Kim et al., PubChem 2023 update, Nucleic Acids Res. 2023, 51, D1373–D1380; PubChem Periodic Table, National Center for Biotechnology Information.

mendeleev.citation: Ł. Mentel, mendeleev – A Python package with properties of chemical elements, ions, isotopes and methods to manipulate and visualize periodic table, version 1.3.0, https://github.com/lmmentel/mendeleev.

pyykko2009.citation: P. Pyykkö, M. Atsumi, Molecular single-bond covalent radii for elements 1–118, Chem. Eur. J. 2009, 15, 186–197 (via mendeleev).

crc2014.citation: W. M. Haynes (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 95th ed., CRC Press, 2014 (via mendeleev).

wikipedia-oxidation.citation: Wikipedia, List of oxidation states of the elements, revision 1102394064 (via mendeleev). Not a peer-reviewed source.

iupac-definition.citation: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements (version 4 May 2022), International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry. Used for atomic number, group, period, and block, which are definitions rather than measured values.

ciaaw-weights-2013.citation: CIAAW, Standard Atomic Weights (2013 edition), www.ciaaw.org, as archived by the Internet Archive on 2015-02-08; J. Meija et al., Atomic weights of the elements 2013 (IUPAC Technical Report), Pure Appl. Chem. 2016, 88, 265–291.

ciaaw-abundances-2009.citation: CIAAW, Isotopic Compositions of the Elements (2009 edition), www.ciaaw.org, as archived by the Internet Archive in 2014; M. Berglund, M. E. Wieser, Isotopic compositions of the elements 2009 (IUPAC Technical Report), Pure Appl. Chem. 2011, 83, 397–410.

ame2012.citation: M. Wang, G. Audi, A. H. Wapstra, F. G. Kondev, M. MacCormick, X. Xu, B. Pfeiffer, The Ame2012 atomic mass evaluation (II), Chin. Phys. C 2012, 36, 1603–2014.

ciaaw-history.citation: CIAAW, per-element pages describing past standard atomic weights, www.ciaaw.org.

ciaaw-abridged-2021.citation: CIAAW, Abridged Standard Atomic Weights 2021, www.ciaaw.org (Internet Archive snapshot, 2023). Earlier edition, shown by the IUPAC 2022 and NIST 2024 periodic tables.
